Where it began

Craig Overton was born in Barnstaple on 10 April 1994 and went to West Buckland School. He has a twin brother, Jamie, who also bowls fast and also played for England, so the Overton household was never short of someone to bowl at.

He came through England's under-19 side, playing 16 youth one-day games between 2011 and 2012, and first played for the Somerset first team in 2012, against Lancashire.

The player

A right-handed batsman and right-arm medium-fast bowler, he was an all-rounder through and through. By 2014 he was a regular for Somerset across every format, and the next summer he was the county's leading wicket-taker in both the Championship and the One-Day Cup. In 2016 he made his maiden first-class hundred, 138 against Hampshire, and his eighth-wicket partnership of 217 that day broke a county record set by Ian Botham and Viv Richards. In 2022 he reached 400 first-class wickets.

His Test debut came at Adelaide in December 2017, in the Ashes, and his first Test wicket was the Australian captain, Steve Smith. Between 2017 and 2022 he played 8 Tests, taking 21 wickets with a best of 3 for 14 and making 182 runs, with a top score of 41 not out. He also played one-day internationals, starting against Australia in June 2018.

What made him special

He offered a bit of everything: steady seam bowling, runs down the order and a willingness to do whatever the side needs. In the 2019 Ashes he was sent in at number three as nightwatchman, a job that asks a bowler to bat like an opener for half an hour. In 2014 he was out for 99 against Lancashire, which says something about his batting, though he might prefer to remember the hundred that came two years later.

Away from the middle

Southern Brave picked him for the first season of The Hundred in 2021, and they bought him again for 2022. In 2026 his fellow professionals voted him the Professional Cricketers' Association Men's Player of the Year, an honour that comes from the people who know the game best.

And finally

Many players can say they got a famous wicket in their first Test. Fewer can say their first one was the opposing captain, in an Ashes Test, in Australia. It set a high bar, and he kept clearing it in county cricket for years afterwards.
